title: UGC 4211: A Confirmed Dual Active Galactic Nucleus in the Local Universe at 230 pc Nuclear Separation
question: Whether the two close-separation (~230 pc) near-IR nuclei in the late-stage major galaxy merger UGC 4211 are both powered by accreting supermassive black holes (a confirmed dual AGN).

data.arrays: 12 m array (46 antennae in C-8, 44 antennae in C-5)
data.angular_resolution: ~0''.06 (0''.061 x 0''.073 for CO cube with robust 0.5; ~0''.07 and ~0''.04 with robust -0.5 for continuum)

what.value: Host galaxy stellar mass log(M*/M_sun)=11.1, molecular gas mass log(M_H2/M_sun)=9.7, and star formation rate log(SFR/M_sun yr^-1)=0.9

evidence.quote: From a compilation study of BAT AGN (cite: Koss:2021:29), the host galaxy was found to be relatively massive compared to nearby galaxies hosting AGN (\log (M_{*}/M_{\odot}) =11.1), with significant molecular gas (\log (M_{H2}/M_{\odot} )=9.7) and a high star formation rate (\log({\rm SFR}/ M_{\odot} \,{\rm yr}^{-1}){=}0.9)

what.value: Chandra and NuSTAR single-nucleus X-ray spectral analysis column density log(N_H/cm^-2)=22.95+/-0.05 and intrinsic luminosity log(L^int_2-10keV/erg s^-1)=43.3

evidence.loc: AGN Bolometric Luminosity, Black Hole Mass, and Eddington ratio
evidence.quote: An X-ray spectral analysis using Chandra (from 2019) and NuSTAR (from 2017) data assuming a single nucleus suggested a moderate column density of \log(N_{\rm H} /{\rm cm}^{-2} )=22.95\pm0.05 (cite: Zhao:2021:A57) with an intrinsic luminosity of \log(L^{\rm int}_{\mathrm{2-10\ keV}} /{\rm erg\,s}^{-1} )=43.3

what.value: Swift/XRT and Swift/BAT X-ray intrinsic luminosity log(L^int_2-10keV/erg s^-1)=42.7+/-0.2

evidence.loc: AGN Bolometric Luminosity, Black Hole Mass, and Eddington ratio
evidence.quote: A previous analysis using Swift/XRT (from 2010) and Swift/BAT data (cite: Ricci:2017:17), had \log(L^{\rm int}_{\mathrm{2-10\ keV}} /{\rm erg\,s}^{-1} )=42.7\pm0.2

what.value: X-Shooter Spectral Library DR2 stellar templates used for pPXF fitting

evidence.quote: We used the X-Shooter Spectral Library (XSL, specifically DR2; (cite: Gonneau:2020:A133)).

what.value: Keck/NIRC2+AO J and K' band imaging

evidence.loc: High Resolution Imaging with HST and Keck
evidence.quote: The Near Infrared Camera 2 (NIRC2)+AO imaging in the J and K^\prime bands (0''04 pix^{-1}) of nearby (z<0.075) hard X-ray selected AGN from the Swift BAT is described in (cite: Koss:2018:214a).

recipe.goal: Measure ALMA 231 GHz nuclear continuum positions, flux densities, separation, and spectral index
recipe.method: Coadd line-free channels in four spectral windows (221-240 GHz) to make high-resolution (~0''.07 and ~0''.04 with robust -0.5) continuum maps, and fit spatial 2D Gaussian models using CASA imfit.
assumptions: Cosmology: Omega_m=0.3, Omega_Lambda=0.7, H_0=70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, scale 0''.69 kpc^-1 at z=0.03474

recipe.goal: Extract and fit optical and NIR nuclear emission line spectra and BPT diagnostics
recipe.method: Extract 1D spectra from HST/STIS (0''.25 x 0''.2), Keck/OSIRIS (0''.3 diameter apertures), and VLT/MUSE (three 0''.15 diameter apertures N, S, M and Voronoi-binned spaxels), fit continuum and Gaussian emission lines, and place line ratios on BPT diagrams.
key_parameters: STIS aperture 5 pixels (0''.25); OSIRIS aperture 0''.3 diameter; MUSE apertures 0''.15 diameter; Voronoi binning S/N=10 for [O III]; 3 pixel median filter on MUSE cube
assumptions: Kewley et al. (2006) strong-line AGN diagnostic classifications

recipe.goal: Measure nuclear stellar kinematics, [O III] kinematics, and ALMA CO(2-1) gas velocity distribution
recipe.method: Fit MUSE Ca II triplet absorption (8350-8900 Å) using pPXF on Voronoi-binned data (S/N=35) and N, S, M apertures; fit [O III] emission velocities; generate ALMA 12CO(2-1) velocity map from 15 km s^-1 channel cube.
key_parameters: CaT region 8350–8900 Å; Voronoi S/N = 35 for stellar kinematics, S/N = 10 for [O III]; ALMA CO(2-1) cube channel width 15 km s^-1, robust = 0.5
assumptions: X-Shooter Spectral Library DR2 stellar templates

recipe.goal: Derive AGN bolometric luminosities, black hole masses, sphere of influence, and Eddington ratios
recipe.method: Convert ALMA nuclear mm luminosity to intrinsic 2-10 keV luminosity using Kawamuro et al. (2022) relation and apply bolometric correction of 20; compute M_BH from broad Pa beta (south) and stellar velocity dispersion sigma_* (north and south); compute Eddington ratios.
key_parameters: Bolometric correction factor = 20 from 2-10 keV luminosity
assumptions: Kawamuro et al. (2022) mm-to-X-ray correlation; den Brok et al. (2022) Pa beta M_BH relation; Kormendy & Ho (2013) M_BH-sigma_* relation; SOI = 33 pc (sigma_*/200 km s^-1)^2.38

recipe.goal: Test for dual X-ray point sources, X-ray variability, and 22 GHz radio continuum counterpart
recipe.method: Fit Chandra image with ChaRT PSF + 2D Gaussian and run BAYMAX to compute Bayes factor for two vs. one point source; analyze Chandra and NuSTAR light curves with XRONOS lcstats; self-calibrate and fit JVLA 22 GHz continuum with CASA imfit.
key_parameters: Chandra subpixel repositioning 0''.25 pix^-1; BAYMAX 20''x20'' box and 1''x1'' prior box; light curve 500s bins; JVLA gaincal solint 180 s
assumptions: Uniform spatial priors on primary and secondary X-ray source positions in BAYMAX (full 20''x20'' FOV or 1''x1'' boxes around IR cores)

recipe.goal: Estimate SMBH binary orbital evolution and hardening timescales
recipe.method: Calculate binary hardening rates due to dynamical friction, stellar hardening, gas-driven inspiral, and GW emission following Goulding et al. (2019) using observed UGC 4211 properties and 230 pc separation.
assumptions: Stellar velocity dispersion estimated from virial theorem; hardening radius a_Hard << G(M_1 + M_2)/sigma_*^2
